profile.name: Ransford Oppong
profile.bio: I am a biomedical engineer and machine learning researcher working across medical imaging, embedded AI, and intelligent sensing. At Université Paris-Saclay and Lab-STICC, IMT Atlantique, I develop hardware-aware medical image segmentation and learned wireless communication systems through the FEF-AI4SD project. My work also spans assistive technologies, multimodal learning, and full-stack software engineering.

news.title: Working on hardware-aware medical image segmentation at Université Paris-Saclay through FEF-AI4SD.
news.summary: Hardware-aware medical AI at Université Paris-Saclay
news.content:
I joined Université Paris-Saclay in September 2026 as a Machine Learning Research Scientist through the France-Ghana FEF-AI4SD project. My research focuses on making medical image segmentation aware of both the dataset and the hardware on which it runs.

My work includes HALO-nnUAP, an automated framework for 2D, 3D, and 4D medical image segmentation. The experimental pipeline covers evaluation across multiple datasets, cross-validation, computational complexity analysis, GPU memory profiling, inference latency, and reproducible experiment tracking with MLflow.

I also develop computational spectroscopy models using FFT and power spectral density analysis to characterize wavelength-dependent spectral signatures. This work is supervised by Professor Daniel Adjei.

news.title: Developing embedded AI and learned communication systems at Lab-STICC, IMT Atlantique.
news.summary: Embedded AI and learned communications at Lab-STICC
news.content:
In September 2026, I began a Research Intern role in Embedded AI at Lab-STICC, IMT Atlantique, in Brest, France, through the France-Ghana FEF-AI4SD project.

I am developing MLPARE-Com, an integrated machine learning framework for joint physical- and link-layer optimization. It combines learned transceiver models, hybrid channel estimation algorithms, and Q-learning-driven retransmission policies.

The embedded testbed uses ESP32-S3 firmware for neural inference, real-time channel sensing, and adaptive ACK/NACK-based reliability control. The evaluation pipeline spans MIMO channel simulation, model training, embedded deployment, and analysis of communication reliability, latency, and computational performance. This work is supervised by Professor Derek Asiedu.

news.title: Presented emotion-aware embedding fusion for mental health counselling at KONVENS 2026 in Hamburg.
news.summary: Presenting emotion-aware embedding fusion at KONVENS 2026
news.content:
I presented “Emotion-Aware Embedding Fusion in Large Language Models for Intelligent Response Generation in Mental Health Counselling” as a poster at KONVENS 2026 in Hamburg, Germany.

The work was co-authored with K. Dotse, A. A. Adjei, J. Arthur, V. Kasore, A. B. Kponyo, J. Agyemang, and J. J. Kponyo.

The conference paper is available through the link below.

news.title: Released a preprint on certified tool execution for MCP-based AI agents.
news.summary: A preprint on certified tool execution for AI agents
news.content:
My October 2026 preprint is titled “Certified Tool Execution Framework for MCP-Based AI Agents: Provably Secure Defense Against Tool Poisoning and Credential Theft.”

The manuscript addresses tool execution security in MCP-based AI agents, with a focus on tool poisoning and credential theft.

Read the preprint using DOI 10.20944/preprints202610.2580.v1, linked below.

news.title: Presented HALO-UNet at TWEEK in Kumasi and ObstaMed at iN4iN in Leipzig.
news.summary: Sharing HALO-UNet and ObstaMed in Kumasi and Leipzig
news.content:
In 2025, I presented two projects in medical AI and assistive technologies.

At TWEEK 2025 in Kumasi, Ghana, I gave oral and poster presentations on “HALO-UNet: A Lightweight Multi-Stage Deep Learning Framework for Thyroid Nodule Segmentation in Low-Resource Ultrasound Imaging,” co-authored with A. J. Anokye and I. Acquah.

At iN4iN 2025 in Leipzig, Germany, I gave an oral presentation on “Obstamed: Smart Obstacle Detection Mobility Aid for the Visually Impaired,” co-authored with G. S. Adjei.
